    # patterns at the top-left and XOR their cells, yielding compact target.
    comps=[]; seen=set()
    for r,c in pts:
        if (r,c) in seen: continue
        stack=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); comp=[]
        while stack:
            y,x=stack.pop(); comp.append((y,x))
            for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                q=(y+dy,x+dx)
                if q not in seen and 0<=q[0]<len(grid) and 0<=q[1]<len(grid[0]) and grid[q[0]][q[1]]:
                    seen.add(q); stack.append(q)
        comps.append(comp)
    # In examples, objects are grouped in three widely-spaced bands. XOR all
    # foreground patterns after normalizing each component's own bounding box.
    shapes=[]
    for comp in comps:
        a=min(y for y,x in comp); b=max(y for y,x in comp); c=min(x for y,x in comp); d=max(x for y,x in comp)
        shapes.append((a,b,c,d,comp))
    # Obtain compact output as XOR overlay of all separated shape instances
    # using their absolute location within the three bands, scaled to common origin.
    h=max(b-a+1 for a,b,c,d,_ in shapes); w=max(d-c+1 for a,b,c,d,_ in shapes)
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for a,b,c,d,comp in shapes:
        for y,x in comp: out[y-a][x-c] ^= grid[y][x]
    return out
